o1.biggest_strength: Finds the top-5 stock-out and fixes it with a rush order, a standard order and re-cartoning, all inside cash (₹1,14,13,400, arithmetic checks) with ₹5.87 lakh held back. It also unloads the glitter palettes through a lipstick add-on and a dated clearance rule.
o1.biggest_mistake: It hands the ops lead conditional homework (move foundation or kohl shades under 8 weeks to rush, a January rule that depends on sales, a liquidator decision) when the owner asked for one plan, and its date-by-date stock table is hard to follow.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the conditionals, give one dated action table and a full back-in-stock message in the brand voice, and trim to 900 words.

o2.biggest_strength: A decisive plan with a clean PO table (₹1.187 crore, arithmetic checks), a cover and ending-stock table that shows why each line gets what it gets, and a dated action list the ops lead can run from Monday.
o2.biggest_mistake: Bundling glitter palettes with kohl uses a line that is itself tight on stock. The 4-per-shade cap also sits awkwardly with bridal artists who buy 6 to 10 units, and it leaves only about ₹1.3 lakh spare.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Pair the palette with the slow-moving lipsticks instead of kohl, exempt pre-booked artists from the cap, and keep a larger cash buffer.

reason: Both catch the top-5 stock-out, use rush plus re-cartoning and stay inside cash. Output 2 is the more decisive single plan, with a plain dated action list and a clearer back-in-stock message. Output 1 has a better palette clearance idea but leaves more conditional homework.
